args.body:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION / NEGOTIATION

MEMORANDUM

TO:      Deal Team / Engagement File (Matter File 20 — International Trade Sanctions)
FROM:    [Counsel]
DATE:    2026
RE:      Counterparty Markup of CFIUS National Security Agreement — Risk-Prioritized Analysis, Recommendations, and Counter-Draft Language

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the counterparty's latest markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement ("NSA") against the base deal materials, the operative schedules and exhibits, and the controlling partner instruction reflected in the most current deal-correspondence thread. The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that must be reconciled against the base materials, the disclosure schedules, and the parties' mandated negotiation priorities:

    (1) a reduction in the indemnification cap, combined with conversion of the 
        indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
    (2) new carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") for 
        regulatory action of precisely the kind at issue in this matter;
    (3) a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core 
        representations, contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Each deviation is analyzed below, ranked by risk to the client, with a stated recommendation and, for each material change, counter-draft language.

Controlling negotiation instruction: Per the most recent partner email (which supersedes any earlier, contrary direction in the thread), the client (a) will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but (b) treats any survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. The memo is drafted to reflect that controlling instruction.

Priority ranking of risks (highest to lowest):
    1. Survival-period reduction (walk-away)
    2. MAE carve-outs for regulatory action
    3. Indemnification cap reduction
    4. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION 1 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
    (WALK-AWAY ISSUE — HIGHEST PRIORITY / REJECT)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations. This directly contradicts Exhibit B, which establishes the survival matrix for the transaction and is a scheduled exhibit that controls over general statements in the base materials (Schedules and Exhibits — International Trade Sanctions). Because Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, the core representations covering regulatory compliance, sanctions, and CFIUS matters are the most exposed to post-closing claims. Shortening their survival materially undermines the client's ability to recover for breaches that may only mature after the abbreviated period lapses.

Under the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. We must therefore hold firm and reject the change outright.

RISK ASSESSMENT: CRITICAL — Deal risk. Conceding any survival-period reduction for the core representations is outside the negotiating mandate and unacceptable.

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT. Restore the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B in its entirety. Do not accept any shortening of survival for the fundamental and core representations and warranties (including those governing regulatory approvals, sanctions compliance, CFIUS representations, and authority), or for the corresponding survival covenants and indemnification claims based on them.

COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE:

    "Survival. The representations and warranties of [Company] contained in this 
    Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the 
    Closing until the date that is [two (2) years] after the Closing Date, and 
    shall thereupon terminate. The Fundamental Representations (including the 
    representations and warranties set forth in [Sections __ (Authority), __ 
    (Regulatory Approvals), __ (Sanctions and Export Controls), and __ (CFIUS)], 
    as applicable) shall survive the Closing indefinitely and shall not expire. 
    All covenants and agreements contained in this Agreement that by their terms 
    require performance after the Closing shall survive the Closing in accordance 
    with their terms. No claim for indemnification for breach of any representation 
    or warranty shall be asserted after the expiration of the applicable survival 
    period set forth in this Section, provided that claims asserted in writing prior 
    to the expiration of such period shall survive until finally resolved. 
    Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall the survival period for any 
    representation or warranty be shorter than the survival period set forth in 
    the survival matrix attached as Exhibit B, which Exhibit is incorporated herein 
    by reference and controls."

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION 2 — MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
    (HIGH RISK — DIRECTLY INTERSECTS SCHEDULE 3.7 / REJECT OR NARROW)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for "regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." This is not a benign technical clarification. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries involving the target. Adding a carve-out for regulatory action would have the effect of excluding from the MAE definition precisely the adverse events (sanctions-related or CFIUS-adjacent regulatory actions) that these pending inquiries could produce. Under the scheduling rule that disclosed exceptions control over general statements, the pending inquiries in Schedule 3.7 are a known, live risk; the MAE carve-out would operate to strip the client of a material-protection mechanism for that exact risk.

RISK ASSESSMENT: HIGH — The carve-out emasculates the MAE definition for the principal regulatory exposure the deal already faces, as documented in Schedule 3.7.

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT the broad regulatory-action carve-out, or at minimum narrow it so it cannot reach regulatory action arising from, related to, or in respect of (a) the pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 or (b) the target's sanctions/export-control or CFIUS compliance. Because this carve-out is directly tied to a known, scheduled exposure, we should resist it vigorously; the client should not cede its MAE protection for the very regulatory risk it has already identified in the schedules.

COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE (narrow the carve-out / add protective proviso):

    "'Material Adverse Effect' means any change, effect, event, circumstance, 
    occurrence or development that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or 
    would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the 
    business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations 
    of the Company, taken as a whole, other than any change, effect, event or 
    occurrence resulting from or arising out of: ...
        (w) any change in Laws, or the interpretation or enforcement thereof, by 
            any Governmental Authority, EXCEPT to the extent such change 
            disproportionately and adversely affects the Company relative to other 
            participants in the industries in which the Company operates; and
        (x) any action, investigation, inquiry, or proceeding taken or commenced 
            by any Governmental Authority, EXCEPT any such action, investigation, 
            inquiry, or proceeding that (i) relates to, arises out of, or is in 
            respect of the regulatory or governmental inquiries disclosed in 
            Schedule 3.7, (ii) relates to, arises out of, or is in respect of any 
            sanctions, export-controls, or CFIUS-related matter, or (iii) arises 
            from any breach of a representation or warranty or failure to comply 
            with any covenant set forth in this Agreement.
    For the avoidance of doubt, none of the foregoing exclusions or carve-outs 
    shall apply to, or operate to exclude, any adverse effect arising from or 
    relating to the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 or any 
    sanctions, export-control, or CFIUS-related regulatory action."

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION 3 — REDUCTION OF THE INDEMNIFICATION CAP
    (HIGH RISK — SILENTLY SHIFTS RETAINED LIABILITIES / RESTORE)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. This reduction is made more consequential by Schedule 5.2, which lists retained liabilities. Absent the markup change, those retained liabilities would be subject to the firm-standard cap. By reducing the cap, the counterparty silently shifts the exposure for those Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities back to the client, capping the counterparty's indemnification obligation at a level lower than needed to cover identified liabilities. Because Schedule 5.2 controls and identifies specific retained liabilities, the reduced cap under-covers them.

RISK ASSESSMENT: HIGH — Reduces the client's recovery for identified (scheduled) liabilities and for breaches of core representations.

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT the cap reduction and restore the firm-standard cap. At a minimum, confirm the cap is sized to cover the aggregate value of the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities plus the full value of fundamental-representation claims.

COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE:

    "Indemnification; Cap. Subject to the other provisions of this Article __, the 
    aggregate liability of [Indemnifying Party] for all claims for indemnification 
    pursuant to [Sections __ (Breach of Representations and Warranties) and __ 
    (Breach of Covenants)] shall not exceed [SPECIFY AMOUNT] (the 'Cap'). The Cap 
    shall not apply to, and shall be calculated exclusive of, any amounts payable 
    in respect of the breach of any Fundamental Representation, any fraud, or any 
    willful misconduct. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, in no 
    event shall the Cap be set at a level less than the aggregate amount of the 
    retained liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2, and the Cap shall be deemed 
    automatically increased to the extent necessary to cover all such scheduled 
    retained liabilities. Nothing in this Section shall be construed to reduce or 
    eliminate the liability reflected in Schedule 5.2."

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. DEVIATION 4 — CONVERSION OF INDEMNITY BASKET FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING
    (LOWER RISK — CLIENT-MANDATED CONCESSION / ACCEPT WITH MINOR PROTECTIONS)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty converts the indemnity basket from a deductible (dollar-for-dollar recovery once the threshold is exceeded, with the full loss only for amounts above and beyond) to a tipping basket (full recovery once the threshold is crossed, but nothing below it). Per the controlling partner instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion. This is, accordingly, an accepted concession and not a walk-away issue.

Although the conversion is conceded, we should seek to (a) preserve the aggregate-basket calculation so the threshold is measured across all claims taken together (not per-claim), (b) ensure claims for fraud and breaches of fundamental representations are excluded from the basket entirely, and (c) resist any increase in the threshold amount alongside the conversion.

RISK ASSESSMENT: MODERATE — Accepted by mandate; implement cleanly to avoid per-claim erosion.

RECOMMENDATION: ACCEPT the deductible-to-tipping conversion consistent with client instruction, but negotiate the following counter-draft to preserve protections and prevent scope creep.

COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE:

    "Basket. [Indemnifying Party] shall not be liable for claims for indemnification 
    pursuant to [Sections __ (Breach of Representations and Warranties) and __ 
    (Breach of Covenants)] unless and until the aggregate amount of all Damages 
    sustained by [Indemnified Party] in respect of all such claims (determined on 
    an aggregate basis across all claims, and not on a per-claim or per-breach 
    basis) exceeds [SPECIFY BASKET AMOUNT] (the 'Basket'), in which event 
    [Indemnifying Party] shall be liable for the FULL amount of all such Damages 
    from the first dollar thereof (it being agreed that the Basket is a 'tipping' 
    basket). Any Damages arising from the breach of any Fundamental Representation, 
    any fraud, or any willful misconduct shall not be subject to, or counted toward, 
    the Basket. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing herein shall reduce or limit 
    the Cap or any amount payable in respect of retained liabilities under 
    Schedule 5.2."

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. RECONCILIATION WITH SCHEDULES, EXHIBITS, AND CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Schedules control over general statements. Pursuant to the scheduling rule in the base materials, the disclosure schedules (including Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2) and Exhibit B are scheduled exceptions that control over general statements in the base agreement. Each of the counterparty's deviations must be tested against these scheduled controls:
     - Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries) intersects the MAE carve-out 
       (Deviation 2). The carve-out must not be permitted to reach these scheduled 
       inquiries.
     - Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities) intersects the indemnification cap 
       reduction (Deviation 3). The cap must be sized to cover the scheduled 
       retained liabilities.
     - Exhibit B (survival matrix) is contradicted by the limitation-period change 
       (Deviation 1). Exhibit B controls; the reduction must be rejected.

B. Controlling partner instruction. Only the most recent email in the deal-correspondence thread controls. It provides that the client (i) concedes the basket conversion and (ii) treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The memo and recommended positions reflect this instruction:
     - Basket conversion: accept (Deviation 4).
     - Survival-period reduction: reject, walk-away if forced (Deviation 1).

C. Sequencing. If negotiation deadlocks on any single point, the walk-away issue (survival-period reduction) is the drop-dead item. The MAE carve-outs and cap reduction, while high risk, are negotiable subject to the counter-draft positions above.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION SUMMARY (BY PRIORITY)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    1. Survival-period reduction (Exhibit B) ......... REJECT — walk-away. Restore Exhibit B matrix.
    2. MAE carve-outs for regulatory action .......... REJECT / NARROW — carve out the Schedule 3.7 
                                                             and sanctions/CFIUS regulatory risk.
    3. Indemnification cap reduction ................. REJECT / RESTORE — size cap to Schedule 5.2 
                                                             retained liabilities.
    4. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping) ...... ACCEPT — per client instruction; keep aggregate 
                                                             basket, exclude fraud/fundamental reps.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. CONCLUSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup, while accepting most firm-standard terms, materially erodes the client's protections in three respects: it shortens survival of the core representations (a walk-away item per the controlling partner instruction and a direct contradiction of Exhibit B), it adds MAE carve-outs for the very regulatory action exposed by the two pending inquiries in Schedule 3.7, and it silently reduces the indemnification cap in a way that under-covers the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. The fourth change — converting the indemnity basket to a tipping basket — is a mandated concession that should be implemented cleanly. We recommend holding firm on the survival-period reduction, resisting/narrowing the MAE carve-outs and cap reduction with the counter-draft language above, and accepting the basket conversion only on the protective terms specified.

Please advise if you would like to adjust the negotiation priorities or re-traffic any of the counter-draft language before the next mark-up cycle.

[counsel]
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
